claim: No board in the 60-board Media section draws `localOnly` — the per-asset flag that decides whether a placed image will publish. Every drawer board shows the same four clean cards.
truth: `localOnly` is a real, persisted MediaAsset field set whenever the server mirror fails (missing blob token, offline, plan size rejection). Its ONLY rendering anywhere in the product is a workspace-wide count pill in the fullpage manager; the 280 drawer — which is where assets are picked and dropped — has no per-asset marker at all, only a warning toast at the moment of insert.
evidence: shared/types/media.ts:182 `localOnly?: boolean`; editor/media/LibraryManager.tsx:170-171 (count) and :449-452 renders `{localOnlyCount} not on the server` — grep for `localOnly` across editor/sidebar/tabs/media returns 6 hits, all in hooks (useUploadState.ts:128, useMediaState.ts:235,:268 toasts) and the mapper (mediaUtils.ts:74); AssetCell.tsx has no localOnly branch (read in full, 211 lines). Server side: publish.service.ts:18-108 runPrePublishChecks builds six checks and none reads image src.
edit: New board `Media · local-only assets` at 280x812 in section 1776:8372, cloned from 144:2. Change: two of the four cards carry a 14h `⚠ device only` marker under the filename (same 40x14 slot the STOCK badge uses at (6,56), warning tint), and a 22h strip under the type-pill row reads `2 files are only on this device — they will not publish.` Add caption board `caption/Media · local-only` at 280x54 beside 155:41.

claim: The one delete-confirm board warns about breaking canvas elements and stops there.
truth: Deleting an asset hard-deletes the Vercel Blob after counting only OTHER MediaAsset/MediaAssetVersion rows sharing the URL — no page or element check exists server-side — and publish hot-links that blob URL verbatim into the deployed HTML. The delete therefore 404s images on the LIVE published site, on a site nobody edited, and a publish rollback restores markup pointing at the same deleted blob.
evidence: server/services/media.service.ts:320 deletes the row, :337-340 counts only asset/version rows, :341-343 `if (otherAssetRefs === 0 && otherVersionRefs === 0) { await del(asset.url); }`; lib/publish-files.ts:53-68 maps p.html through five string injectors and never touches src attributes; publish.service.ts:340 retains the markup in PublishBuildJob.log. The editor's own guard MediaCommandLayer.deleteWithGrace (:88-133) only clears srcs in the current session's document. Filed as MOD-E-04.
edit: On 1175:4827, add a second warning block under the existing `⚠ N files are currently used on the canvas` block: a red-tint 44h band reading `N of these are live on your published site. Deleting removes the file from storage — those images will break.` Also add the in-use FILE→PAGE list the code already renders (ConfirmDeleteModal.tsx:77-86 prints `filename — page, page`), which no board draws.

claim: The versions drill-in draws an inline 32h restore confirm and nothing about consequences.
truth: Restoring a version repoints the LIBRARY at the new URL and leaves every placed element on the old one. The same component computes the usage-by-page list eleven lines later and offers a jump-to-element handler, so it knows exactly which elements it is about to orphan. Its sibling surface does it correctly (AssetDetailsPanel calls replaceAcross).
evidence: AssetDetailOverlay.confirmRestore (:140-155) calls `restoreAssetVersion(versionId).then(res => onUpdate?.(item.key, { src: res.url }))` and nothing else; collectUsageByPage at :158-166; the correct sibling is AssetDetailsPanel.tsx:234 `composer.mediaOps.replaceAcross(versions[0].src, v.src)`. Server rewrites the parent asset url+bytes at media.service.ts:477-480 without snapshotting the outgoing URL (:457-481), so restore is one-way. Filed as MOD-E-20.
edit: In the 32h inline confirm band on 146:32, replace the bare `Restore` / `Cancel` pair with confirm copy that names the consequence: `Restore this version? It is used in 3 places — those will update too.` Add a sibling board `Media · drill-in · versions · restore-confirm` (280x812) cloned from 146:32 with the band open, since no board currently shows the band in its open state.

claim: The icon picker inserts an icon on the canvas with defaults and pops back to the grid.
truth: Inserting an icon produces an element that cannot render. All three call sites pass the icon NAME as the src, insertMediaAt maps type `icon` to element type `icon`, and TYPE_TO_TAG_MAP maps `icon` to a bare `span` — so the document gets `<span src="User">` and shows nothing, under a green success toast. The icon definitions already carry a usable `svgDataUrl` that these call sites ignore.
evidence: MediaTab.tsx:218 `composer.mediaOps.insertMedia(icon.name, "icon")`, MediaTab.tsx:401 (IconBrowserOverlay onPick), LibraryManager.tsx:206 — each followed by a `${icon.name} icon added ✓` toast; ElementManager.ts:434 maps icon→"icon"; shared/utils/html/typeMapping.ts:159 maps icon→"span"; MediaManager.ts:93 DiscIcon carries svgDataUrl. Searched engine/ for icon-specific serialization by constant and by tag name: only MediaManager.ts:59. Filed as MOD-E-15.
edit: Rename board 147:2 to `NOT IMPLEMENTED — inserted icons render as an empty <span>; the picker works, the result is invisible`. Add the note to caption 155:45, second sentence. Do not change the drawn design — the picker itself is correct and the fix is one line in the call sites.

claim: The replace-across result is a 948x80 strip of result states.
truth: replaceAcross commits PARTIAL batches: it applies what it can, emits REPLACE_PARTIAL with the failed element list, and no UI subscribes — the caller reads only `result.clean`. So the user is told the replace succeeded while N elements still show the old image. The strip is also the wrong object for the job (already filed as W-A-15).
evidence: MediaCommandLayer.ts:262-267 emits REPLACE_PARTIAL with `{ oldSrc, newSrc, succeeded, failed }`; the comment at :270 says `the UI should display` it. Measured listener counts by grepping `on(MEDIA_EVENTS.X)` across src/ excluding tests: REPLACE_PARTIAL=0, REPLACE_OPENED=0, REPLACE_COMMITTED=0, REPLACE_ROLLED_BACK=0, INSERT_SUCCEEDED=0, INSERT_FAILED=0, UPLOAD_START=0. LIBRARY_OPENED (constants/media.ts:148) is neither emitted nor listened to. Filed as MOD-E-09.
edit: Promote the partial case to a real modal state at 520x300 (matching 1164:4738), named `Media · modal · replace-across · partial`: `Replaced on 7 of 9 places.` over a list of the two that failed with their page names, and a `Retry the 2 that failed` action. The 948x80 strip stays as the spec sheet it is; see W-A-15 for its own adjudication.

claim: The failure row reads `Upload failed — file is 24 MB, limit is 10 MB`.
truth: Three different limits are enforced on the way to that row and 10 MB is only one of them, for one plan. The drawer's own pre-flight refuses anything over 50 MB flat with different copy and never reaches this row at all. 10 MB is the FREE plan's server cap; PRO and BUSINESS are clamped to 50 MB. The engine's own validator allows 100 MB for video.

The picker modal states a fourth figure: MediaLibraryPanel.tsx:368 `Upload tab accepts image/video/audio · max 10 MB each`. Related but distinct from W-A-20 (fullpage's `500 MB total`) and MOD-E-16 (engine-vs-server ceiling).

Add to caption 155:37: `The limit is per plan (FREE 10 MB / PRO 50 MB). Anything over 50 MB is refused before it reaches this row — see the pre-flight rejection state, W-A-42.`

MediaTab passes `searchFailed`; LibraryManager does not, so a stock search that fails from the fullpage library falls straight through to `No photos found for "x"` — the exact false negative this state was built to remove, still live on the bigger surface.

Add a note to it: `Reachable from the 280 drawer only — the fullpage library's stock modal is mounted without searchFailed and still shows "No photos found" for a failed request (LibraryManager.tsx:467-486).` This is the scope note the board needs; the design itself is correct.

claim: The stock browser carries a provider switch (Unsplash / Pexels / Pixabay) and a monthly search-quota strip.
truth: W-A-21 and W-A-22 established that no mount site supplies either prop. The deeper fact is that wiring them would not make the switch work: `StockService.searchPhotos` accepts `extras.source` and never forwards it to the tRPC query, and the server proxy has no `source` parameter and no Pixabay implementation at all — photos are always Unsplash, videos are always Pexels. Pixabay exists in three type unions and nowhere else.
evidence: StockService.ts:25 `type StockSource = "unsplash" | "pexels" | "pixabay"`, :30 `Provider override; defaults to "unsplash"`, then :75-78 sends `{ query, page, orientation, color }` — `source` is dropped on the floor. server/services/stock.service.ts:49-54 `searchStockPhotos(query, page, orientation, color)` reads only `process.env.UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY`; :98-102 `searchStockVideos(query, page)` reads only `PEXELS_API_KEY`. useDiscoveryState.ts:106-107 passes `source: discSource` into the call that discards it. Grep for `pixabay` across server/ returns zero hits.
edit: Rename 1716:8557 to `NOT IMPLEMENTED — the provider switch is inert (source is dropped in transport) and the quota number has no producer`. Keep the design. Add a note under the pills: `Photos always come from Unsplash, videos from Pexels; Pixabay is unimplemented server-side.` Cites W-A-21, W-A-22.

claim: `No photos found for "x"` is the empty-result state.
truth: It is also the NOT-CONFIGURED state. When UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY or PEXELS_API_KEY is unset the server returns `[]`, which is byte-identical to a genuine empty result, so an unconfigured deploy looks exactly like a bad search term. A configured-ness signal was deliberately removed because the flag it read was hardcoded true, and the note says a real one needs a server capability endpoint that does not exist.
evidence: server/services/stock.service.ts:55-56 `const key = process.env.UNSPLASH_ACCESS_KEY; if (!key || !query.trim()) return [];` and :102-103 the same for PEXELS_API_KEY; the file header states the intent at :4-6. StockService.ts:53-57 `The server returns [] when its provider keys are unset — the "no results" empty state handles that. (An IS_STOCK_CONFIGURED flag + not-configured banner existed here but was hardcoded true and unreachable; removed 2026-07-25.)`

Mark it as blocked on a server capability endpoint in its caption, since the editor currently cannot tell the two cases apart.

claim: quota-full is drawn as a consequence of the storage bar crossing 100%.
truth: That is the only way to reach it. The engine throws a typed MediaQuotaError carrying `rescueAction: "show-quota-banner"` and emits QUOTA_EXCEEDED, and MediaManager's own comment claims the library banner subscribes. Nothing subscribes. The error lands as a rejection inside Promise.allSettled and surfaces as `N uploads failed` — so a user who fills their storage mid-upload gets a generic failure and never sees this screen.
evidence: MediaManager.ts:848-849 comment `Emits QUOTA_EXCEEDED (the library banner subscribes)`; grep `on(MEDIA_EVENTS.QUOTA_EXCEEDED)` across src/ returns 0. StorageQuotaBar.tsx:45 is a pure props component `({used, total, onOptimize, compact})`. MediaStorageTypes.ts:57-72 MediaQuotaError with rescueAction; thrown at MediaManager.ts:859; caught into useUploadState.ts:190-196 and reported at :207-209 as `${failed} upload${...} failed`. Only the click-insert path names it (useMediaState.ts:288 `Storage full — delete unused assets to free space`). Filed as MOD-E-10.
edit: Add a board `Media · quota-full · hit-during-upload` at 280x812 cloned from 145:250, showing the exhausted quota band ABOVE a failed-upload row whose reason reads `Not enough storage`. This is the screen the code intends and cannot currently produce; boarding it makes the missing subscription visible as a gap rather than as a generic failure.

claim: Folders have one board: creating one inline.
truth: Folders support create, rename, delete and move-asset-into, and only create is drawn. Rename is the one that visibly fails: renameFolder emits FOLDER_UPDATED and nothing listens, while its two siblings FOLDER_CREATED and FOLDER_DELETED are both subscribed — so the old name stays on screen until the panel remounts. Moving a FOLDER (as opposed to moving assets into one) has a server procedure with no caller at all.
evidence: MediaManager.ts:1471 `this.emit(MEDIA_EVENTS.FOLDER_UPDATED, updated);`; useLibraryState.ts subscribes reloadFolders to FOLDER_CREATED and FOLDER_DELETED only — measured listener counts FOLDER_CREATED=1, FOLDER_DELETED=1, FOLDER_UPDATED=0. shared/types/media.ts:265 `renameFolder(serverId, name)` on RemoteAssetSync. media.moveFolder has no caller (W-CO-04). Filed as MOD-E-11.
edit: Add `Media · fullpage · folders · rename (inline)` at 240x330 cloned from 1205:4829 — same inline field, pre-filled with the current name, committed on Enter — and `Media · fullpage · folders · delete-confirm` naming where the assets go (the server cascades folder assets to root, shared/types/media.ts:236-238). Note on the rename board: `The tree does not refresh today — FOLDER_UPDATED has no listener.`

claim: `Type pills are a multi-select filter, each carrying its own count.`
truth: True as far as it goes, and it hides two things. (1) A pill whose count is 0 is rendered DISABLED with a reason, because a filter whose only outcome is the empty state is a dead end — an ACTIVE pill stays enabled at zero so the user can clear it. (2) The four buckets are image / video / svg / icon, and `icon` is the FONT bucket while `svg` is the icon-and-SVG bucket; AUDIO has no pill at all despite being a first-class MediaAssetType the fullpage uploader accepts. Board 145:359 makes this checkable and fails it: all four pills read count `0` there and all four are drawn in the live label ink #111827, where the code would render every one of them disabled.
evidence: TypePills.tsx:72 `const isDeadFilter = !discMode && count === 0 && !isActive;` with :81-82 `disabled={isDeadFilter} title={..."No ${p.label} files in this library yet"}`; :40-45 PILLS maps `ico→"svg"` and `fnt→"icon"`, four entries, no audio. shared/types/media.ts:16 `MediaAssetType = "image"|"video"|"audio"|"icon"|"svg"|"font"`; mediaUtils.ts:121-122 counts only ico/fnt. Measured on 145:359: the four pill labels (`image`,`video`,`svg`,`icon`) carry fill #111827 opacity 1 with counts `0` in #4b5563 — the same treatment 144:2 gives its non-zero pills.
edit: Caption 155:34: append `A pill at zero renders disabled with the reason; an active pill stays enabled at zero so it can be cleared. There is no audio pill — audio has no bucket in the drawer.` On 145:359, draw all four pills in the disabled state (they are all at zero there). On 145:2, draw one pill disabled so the non-empty case carries it too.

claim: W-A-18 filed this board as promising audio uploads the server rejects, on the strength of the client accept-list letting audio through.
truth: Half of that is right and the half about the client is only right for THIS surface. There are three upload doors with three different accept-lists, and they disagree: the fullpage manager accepts audio, the picker modal accepts audio, and the 280 drawer — the surface eleven boards in this section describe — refuses it before it leaves the browser. The server allow-list carries no audio type at all, and audio also never gets `localOnly` set, so none of the five device-only warnings can fire for it.
evidence: Drawer: UploadZone.tsx:15 `ACCEPT_TYPES = "image/*,video/*,.ttf,.otf,.woff,.woff2,.svg"` and :18-24 `isAccepted` has image/video/font branches and no audio — an .mp3 flashes `"x" type not allowed` at :71. Fullpage: LibraryManager.tsx:462 `accept="image/*,video/*,audio/*,.svg,.ttf,.otf,.woff,.woff2"`. Picker: MediaLibraryPanel.tsx:269 `accept="image/*,video/*,audio/*"`. Server: app/api/asset-upload/route.ts:31-50 — no audio entry. localOnly: MediaManager.ts:60-61 toServerAssetType returns null for audio, so the `if (this.remoteSync && serverType)` block at :962 is skipped and the flag is never assigned (MOD-E-13). Engine still admits five audio MIME types at shared/constants/media.ts:51.
edit: Amend W-A-18's note on 1163:13948 rather than adding a second: `Three accept-lists, three contracts — the fullpage and picker take audio, the 280 drawer refuses it in the browser, the server allow-list has no audio type, and an audio asset never gets the localOnly flag the device-only warnings read.` Add the same note to caption 155:36.

claim: The hub draws preview + `2400×1600 · 840 KB`, alt text with ✨ Generate, then five rows.
truth: The alt-text block is missing the half the code renders: when alt text came from the AI generator the panel shows its provenance — `AI-generated by {model} on {date}` — and a Regenerate action. And the provenance is device-local: it is written to IndexedDB, read by the badge, and never synced or rebuilt from the server, even though the Prisma column exists — so the same asset shows the line on the machine that uploaded it and nothing anywhere else.

Written at useAltTextAutoTrigger.ts:65-71. NOT synced: AssetUploadService.ts:193-200 sends only filename and altText; MediaManager.importServerAssets (:490-522) constructs the asset without it; media_assets.generatedMetadata exists (schema.prisma:1026) and the router never touches it. Filed as MOD-E-07.

claim: A font uploads the same way an image does and joins the library.
truth: A font is the one asset type that cannot be placed. insertMediaAt routes type `font` to a font-family application on selected text and fails with `no-text-selected` otherwise. The guidance that would tell the user this after an upload cannot fire: the toast reads `p.mimeType` and the UPLOAD_COMPLETE payload has no such key — the MIME type lives at `p.asset.mimeType` — so a font upload falls through to the generic `File uploaded ✓`, and the instruction survives only on a later click of an already-uploaded font.
evidence: useUploadState.ts:126 `if (p?.mimeType?.includes("font"))`; the emit is MediaManager.ts:1051-1055 `{ success: true, asset: finalAsset, fileName: file.name }`. claim: The library is the workspace's asset store and the fullpage manager is its home.
truth: The library is NOT part of the project. `exportProject()` hardcodes `assets: []` and nothing in the codebase ever reads `data.assets`, so a project export, a version snapshot and a restore all carry zero asset references. The library survives only via this browser's IndexedDB plus the server row — which means an export handed to someone else, or a version restored on another machine, loses every asset reference silently.
evidence: engine/Composer.ts:616 `assets: [],` — grep for `assets` in Composer.ts returns exactly that one line (MOD-E-01 cited :608; the file has since shifted). shared/types/project.ts:40 `assets: AssetData[];` and shared/types/asset.ts:13 AssetData have zero readers and zero writers. Persistence is IndexedDBAdapter.ts:13-21 (db `aquibra-media` v1, stores assets/folders/blobs) plus Prisma media_assets (schema.prisma:1015), which has no FK to Site or User (MOD-E-21).
edit: Add a caption board `caption/Media · fullpage · library` at 1440x54 beside 1159:4593 stating the persistence contract in one line: `The library lives in this browser's IndexedDB and in the workspace's server rows. It is NOT part of a project export or a version snapshot — ProjectData.assets is written empty (Composer.ts:616).` This is the single most load-bearing untold fact in the section and it belongs where a designer draws "restore" and "export".

claim: Upload states are: in progress, failed with a reason, quota-warn, quota-full.
truth: One failure mode is missing and it is the one that misleads. When the server mirror fails for ANY reason — missing BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN, an auth failure, a plan size rejection — uploadAndCreate returns null, MediaManager reads null as "offline", marks the asset localOnly and queues a retry. For a size rejection that retry will fail forever, and for a misconfigured deploy the user is told they are offline when the site's storage is simply not set up. Nothing on screen distinguishes these from a network drop.
evidence: AssetUploadService.ts:136-139 catches everything and returns null; MediaManager.ts:1039-1041 reads null as offline → localOnly + retry queue. Route behaviour: app/api/asset-upload/route.ts mints the token via handleUpload (:21); a missing token throws into the catch at :257 whose mapping (:260-263) matches neither `Unauthenticated` nor `quota`/`limit`, returning 400. app/api/upload/[fileId]/route.ts:70 `put()` returns 500 `Blob upload failed` (:78-81). Filed as MOD-E-16, MOD-E-22.
edit: Add a board `Media · upload · saved-to-this-device-only` at 280x812 cloned from 145:96: the upload row resolves not to a green tick but to an amber row `pasta-2.jpg saved to this device only — it will not publish` with a `Retry upload` link, plus the ⚠ device-only marker on the new card. This is the state the product actually produces most often when storage is misconfigured and the one no board draws.
